risks.note: MD&A 'Risk and Concerns': companies making stainless steel strips, tubes and pipes 'had faced major challenges due to slowdown in the growth of steel industry. The falling demand, low prices, cost escalation in inputs, reduction in import duty are some of the major threats to the sustainability of the Indian Steel Industry.' This is management's own flagged threat list, not an industry aside.
risks.risk: Steel-industry demand slowdown with falling prices

risks.note: MD&A states 'Further reduction in import duty stimulated the import of steel from China and other countries manufacturers at low prices leading to decrease in demand of domestic goods' — a direct volume and pricing threat to the Company's domestic sales.
risks.risk: Low-priced imports following reduction in import duty

risks.note: Named by management as one of the major threats to the sustainability of the Indian Steel Industry; the Company gives no hedging, pass-through or contract-structure mitigation anywhere in the routed text.

MD&A: overcapacity 'growing at its fastest rate in 15 years, threatening to exceed 680 million tons by end-2025, triggering one of the deepest crises since 2009'; China is 'flooding the market with over 100 million tonnes of competitive steel products, impacting global pricing and leading to increased trade barriers.'
risks.risk: Global overcapacity and Chinese export flooding

risks.note: MD&A 'Key Risks and Focus Areas': 'Rising trade barriers and tariffs are reshaping global flow, creating concerns over protectionism.' Combined with the import-duty point above, the Company is exposed to policy moves in both directions.
MD&A: 'Steel prices remain volatile, influenced by fluctuating raw material costs, high energy prices in Europe, and sluggish demand in the construction sector.'
risks.risk: Steel price volatility driven by raw material and energy costs

risks.note: Flagged twice, verbatim in both the India and the global sections: 'More importantly war between Iran and USA, Israel will be key risk factors impacting the economic activities. Oil price will have major impact in the country's growth.'

STRUCTURAL GOVERNANCE RISK stated by the Company itself and repeated identically in the MD&A and the Directors' Report: 'Your Company has adequate internal control systems commensurate with its size and operations, although not documented. The Company regularly gets its accounts audited from internal auditor.' The AR discloses no risk management committee and no ERM framework.
